hints: Focus on what NaOH does differently in water versus in ethanol, substitution versus elimination.
Remember aqueous NaOH provides lots of OH- for nucleophilic substitution to make an alcohol from bromoethane.
Connect ethanolic NaOH to removal of HBr to form a C=C double bond, then check which two statements fit that pattern.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two competing reactions**

Think of bromoethane as able to do two things. It can swap Br for OH, or it can lose HBr altogether.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{substitution or elimination}$$

**Apply aqueous conditions**

In water, NaOH is aqueous and acts as a nucleophile. OH- attacks carbon and replaces Br in a substitution reaction.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{NaOH(aq)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{NaBr}$$

**Apply ethanolic conditions**

In ethanol, NaOH is ethanolic and acts as a base. It removes H from the adjacent carbon with loss of Br in an elimination reaction.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{NaOH(ethanolic)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{NaBr} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Judge statements 1, 2 and 3**

Statement 1 claims a diol with two OH groups, impossible from $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ which has only one Br to replace. Statement 2 correctly gives ethene by elimination, and statement 3 correctly gives ethanol by substitution. So only 2 and 3 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect if this option includes statement 1. Ethane-1,2-diol needs two OH groups, but bromoethane has only one Br to substitute, so aqueous NaOH can only give ethanol with one OH group.
options.B: Incorrect if this option includes statement 1 with statement 2 but omits statement 3. Statement 1 is false, while statement 3 is true and should not be left out, as aqueous NaOH gives ethanol by nucleophilic substitution.
options.C: Correct for 2 and 3 only. Statement 2 is true because ethanolic NaOH causes dehydrohalogenation to ethene. Statement 3 is true because aqueous NaOH causes hydrolysis to ethanol. Statement 1 is false.
options.D: Incorrect if this is statement 3 only. Statement 3 alone is true, but it is incomplete because statement 2 is also true. Ethanolic NaOH with bromoethane does give ethene as the main elimination product.
